newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on USDA ending stocks data.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on USDA ending stocks data.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower after USDA raised its estimate of 1996/97 end stocks, traders said.
Wheat also was dragged lower by spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans, which sank on similar bearishness over USDA's forecast for soybean ending stocks.
In its May report, USDA raised its wheat end stocks estimate by five million bushels to 465 million.
"The stocks number was the trigger for all the markets," a KCBT trader said. "We were essentially a follower... and just played catch-up with Chicago."
But scale-down buying by locals and commission houses enabled KCBT wheat to close relatively firmer than its counterparts in Chicago and Minneapolis.
KCBT wheat settled seven to 12 cents per bushel lower, with new crop July down 10 cents at $4.24-1/2.

Commission house Refco was a featured name on both sides of the players' sheet, buying 2.5 million July but also selling two million July, traders said. Linnco sold 2.3 million July and Continental bull-spread one million July/December bushels at nine cents, floor sources said.
